deck_name: 16 - Predict the Exact Output Gauntlet v2 (C++, C#, Python, Java, JS)

cards.explanation: p points to arr[1] (20). *(p + 2) accesses arr[3] (40), and p[-1] accesses arr[0] (10).
Usual arithmetic conversions promote signed int b (-2) to unsigned int (UINT_MAX - 1), causing unsigned wraparound > 0.
struct is a value type in C#. Assigning p1 to p2 copies the struct by value, so mutating p2.X leaves p1.X unchanged.
Strings in C# are immutable reference types. b += "!" allocates a new string and updates reference b while a still points to "hello".

cards.code:
def append_item(val, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(val)
    return bucket

print(append_item(1), append_item(2))
cards.explanation: Default mutable arguments in Python are evaluated once at function definition time, so both calls mutate and return the same list.
nums[1:4] produces [20, 30, 40], and [::-1] reverses that slice into [40, 30, 20].

cards.code:
a = [1, 2]
b = a
a = a + [3]
print(b)
cards.explanation: a = a + [3] creates a new list object and rebinds a, whereas b still references the original [1, 2] list (unlike a += [3]).
Java's Integer cache pools boxed values from -128 to 127 (same object reference), whereas 128 creates two distinct Integer instances.
The finally block executes before the method returns, and a return inside finally overrides the pending return from try.
Without a compareFn, Array.prototype.sort() converts elements to UTF-16 strings and sorts lexicographically ('10' comes before '2').
Detaching obj.getVal loses its receiver context (`this` becomes undefined in strict mode / global object without .val).
Logical OR (||) treats 0 as falsy and returns 'A'; nullish coalescing (??) only falls back on null or undefined, preserving 0.
References cannot be reseated after initialization; r = y assigns the value of y (10) into x.
Passing x with the `ref` modifier passes a managed reference to x's storage location, updating x to 5.
dict.get() returns the default fallback (99) without inserting the missing key into the dictionary.
Array destructuring binds a = 10 and gathers the remaining 3 elements [20, 30, 40] into rest.
Java Strings are immutable; s.toUpperCase() returns a new String that was ignored rather than reassigned to s.
